title: Naturally occurring cancer-associated mutations disrupt oligomerization and activity of protein arginine methyltransferase 1 (PRMT1).
authors: Price, Owen M; Thakur, Abhishek; Ortolano, Ariana; Towne, Arianna; Velez, Caroline; Acevedo, Orlando; Hevel, Joan M
one_liner_zh: 该文研究PRMT1蛋白二聚化突变对甲基转移酶活性的影响，虽涉及分子动力学模拟，但核心是蛋白-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与TF-DNA结合机制课题关联较弱。
abstract: Protein arginine methylation is a posttranslational modification catalyzed by the protein arginine methyltransferase (PRMT) enzyme family. Dysregulated protein arginine methylation is linked to cancer and a variety of other human diseases. PRMT1 is the predominant PRMT isoform in mammalian cells and acts in pathways regulating transcription, DNA repair, apoptosis, and cell proliferation. PRMT1 dimer formation, which is required for methyltransferase activity, is mediated by interactions between a structure called the dimerization arm on one monomer and a surface of the Rossman Fold of the other monomer. Given the link between PRMT1 dysregulation and disease and the link between PRMT1 dimerization and activity, we searched the Catalogue of Somatic Mutations in Cancer (COSMIC) database to identify potential inactivating mutations occurring in the PRMT1 dimerization arm. We identified three mutations that correspond to W215L, Y220N, and M224V substitutions in human PRMT1V2 (isoform 1) (W197L, Y202N, M206V in rat PRMT1V1). Using a combination of site-directed mutagenesis, analytical ultracentrifugation, native PAGE, and activity assays, we found that these conservative substitutions surprisingly disrupt oligomer formation and substantially impair both S-adenosyl-L-methionine (AdoMet) binding and methyltransferase activity. Molecular dynamics simulations suggest that these substitutions introduce novel interactions within the dimerization arm that lock it in a conformation not conducive to dimer formation. These findings provide a clear, if putative, rationale for the contribution of these mutations to impaired arginine methylation in cells and corresponding health consequences.
abstract_zh: 蛋白质精氨酸甲基化是由蛋白质精氨酸甲基转移酶（PRMT）酶家族催化的一种翻译后修饰。蛋白质精氨酸甲基化的失调与癌症及多种其他人类疾病相关。PRMT1是哺乳动物细胞中主要的PRMT亚型，参与调控转录、凋亡、细胞增殖等通路的调节。PRMT1二聚体的形成是甲基转移酶活性所必需的，该过程由一个单体上的二聚化臂结构与另一个单体上的Rossman折叠表面之间的相互作用介导。鉴于PRMT1失调与疾病之间的关联，以及PRMT1二聚化与活性之间的联系，我们检索了癌症体细胞突变目录（COSMIC）数据库，以识别PRMT1二聚化臂中可能发生的失活突变。我们鉴定出三个突变，分别对应人PRMT1V2（异构体1）中的W215L、Y220N和M224V替换（大鼠PRMT1V1中的W197L、Y202N、M206V）。通过结合定点突变、分析超速离心、天然PAGE和活性测定，我们发现这些保守替换意外地破坏了寡聚体的形成，并显著损害了S-腺苷-L-甲硫氨酸（AdoMet）结合及甲基转移酶活性。分子动力学模拟表明，这些替换在二聚化臂内引入了新的相互作用，将其锁定在不利于二聚体形成的构象中。这些发现为这些突变导致细胞中精氨酸甲基化受损及相应的健康后果提供了明确（尽管是推测性的）解释依据。
